description: 1.18/1.19/1.20 fork of the Forge Client Reset Packet Updated

mods.name: Client Reset Packet
mods.description: Adds a reset packet to Minecraft Forge to allow Modern Forge (1.13+) support on proxies.

releases.notes:
## ForgeClientResetPacket 0.1.2 – Forge 1.18.2

Changes since 0.1.1:

### Oculus shaders workaround (#3, possibly #12)
- Oculus shaders are switched off on the render thread just before the client reset, and turned back on about 2 seconds (40 ticks) after you land on the new server. This works around the "Failed to clear, closing connection" kick when switching servers with shaders on.
- If the switch fails, shaders come back on at the title, multiplayer or disconnected screen.
- Shaders are only turned back on if they're still off the way the mod left them. If you changed the shader setting during the switch, your choice is kept.
- A shutdown hook restores your Oculus config if the game closes mid-switch.
- The restore always runs on the render thread, and a failed restore is retried (up to 3 times) instead of silently leaving shaders off.
- Soft dependency through the public Iris/Oculus API only (Oculus 1.2.5–1.6.4 for 1.18.2). Nothing changes when Oculus isn't installed.
- Toasts appear when shaders are paused, restored, or when restore fails.

### Fixes
- The negotiating screen now uses the translated `connect.negotiating` string (the previous build used a 1.19.2-only type and could not compile).
- The server resource pack is kept across the reset.
- Leftover Forge packet filters (`forge:forge_fixes`, `forge:vanilla_filter`) are removed after clearing, and already-present filters are skipped on re-injection, so the next handshake doesn't fail.
- If the connection drops mid-reset (e.g. mismatched mods), you get the disconnect reason instead of hanging on "Negotiating...".
- The `isNecessary` invoker on Forge's packet filter is marked `remap = false`.

### Packaging
- mods.toml version comes from the build; Minecraft `[1.18.2,1.19)`, Forge `[40,41)`.
- Project links point to FoxyCraftNetwork.
- `pack.mcmeta` uses pack_format 8 (1.18.2 resource format).
- English and Chinese (zh_cn) translations for player-facing text.

Client-side only. Minecraft **1.18.2 only** (not 1.18 or 1.18.1). PR: https://github.com/FoxyCraftNetwork/Forge-Client-Reset-Packet/pull/35

## ForgeClientResetPacket 0.3.2 – Forge 1.20 / 1.20.1

Changes since 0.3.1:

### Oculus shaders workaround (#3, possibly #12)
- Oculus shaders are switched off on the render thread just before the client reset, and turned back on about 2 seconds (40 ticks) after you land on the new server. This works around the "Failed to clear, closing connection" kick when switching servers with shaders on.

- Shaders are only turned back on if they're still off the way the mod left them. If you changed the shader setting during the switch, your choice is kept.
- A shutdown hook restores your Oculus config if the game closes mid-switch.
- The restore always runs on the render thread, and a failed restore is retried (up to 3 times) instead of silently leaving shaders off.
- Soft dependency through the public Iris/Oculus API only. Nothing changes when Oculus isn't installed.

### Fixes
- mods.toml now declares Minecraft `[1.20,1.20.2)` and Forge `[46.0.14,48)`, so 1.20.2 no longer tries to load this jar and crash with `NoClassDefFoundError: NetworkConstants`.

Client-side only. PR: https://github.com/FoxyCraftNetwork/Forge-Client-Reset-Packet/pull/14

mods.name: Client Reset Packet
mods.description:
Makes proxy server switches (Velocity and similar) behave like a clean reconnect on modern Forge clients.

On Minecraft 1.20.2+ the proxy switches servers through the vanilla configuration phase. This mod resets the client-side Forge state that a real disconnect would reset (registries, network channel state, logout/level-unload events) and pauses Oculus/Iris shaders across the switch.

releases.notes:
## ForgeClientResetPacket 0.4.0 – Forge 1.21.6 to 1.21.11

First release of ForgeClientResetPacket for this Minecraft line.

Client-side only: put it in the client `mods/` folder. The backend servers behind Velocity need [Proxy-Compatible-Forge](https://modrinth.com/mod/proxy-compatible-forge).

### How it works on 1.20.2+
- From 1.20.2, Velocity switches servers by sending the vanilla start-configuration packet, and Forge re-runs its handshake in the configuration phase. The old login-phase reset packet no longer exists.
- When that happens, the mod does the cleanup Forge normally only does on a real disconnect: it fires the logout and level-unload events, reverts registries to their frozen state, and resets the connection's Forge network state so the next backend gets a clean handshake.
- Each Forge `NetworkContext` member is reset on its own. A field missing on your Forge build is skipped instead of aborting the whole reset (e.g. `remoteChannelsSize`, missing on many builds).

### Also included
- Oculus/Iris shader pause from 0.3.2: shaders turn off before the switch and come back on after you land, or on the title/disconnected screen if the switch fails. Your own shader setting is respected. Nothing changes without Oculus.
- English and Chinese (zh_cn) translations for player-facing text. The Chinese text still needs a native-speaker review.

### This build
- One jar for 1.21.6 through 1.21.11 (Forge 56+, Java 21), using Forge's EventBus 7 listeners.
- The loading-terrain screen is matched by class name, so the jar works both before and after its 1.21.9 rename.
- `pack.mcmeta` carries both the older format keys and the 1.21.9+ `min_format`/`max_format` keys.

PR: https://github.com/FoxyCraftNetwork/Forge-Client-Reset-Packet/pull/27
